# HW 9 - Basic Modeling Practice

## Read the bike data

This data set is about bike sharing rentals

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(rsample)
bike_data <- read_csv("https://www4.stat.ncsu.edu/~online/datasets/SeoulBikeData.csv",locale = locale(encoding="latin1"))
bike_data


```

## EDA

### Check for missingness

```{r}
colSums(is.na(bike_data))

```

### check column types/sanity-check values

```{r}
sapply(bike_data, class)
summary(bike_data |> select(where(is.numeric)))
unique(bike_data$Seasons)
unique(bike_data$Holiday)
unique(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)

```

### Parse the data, rename columns to snake_case, covert categoricals to factors

```{r}

bike <- bike_data 
names(bike) <- c("date","rented_count","hour","temp", "humidity","wind_speed","visibility","dew_point_temp","solar_radiation",
                 "rainfall","snowfall","seasons","holiday","functioning_day")

bike <- bike |>
  mutate(date = dmy(date)) |>
  mutate(across(c(seasons, holiday, functioning_day), as.factor))

bike

```

### Summary stats on rented_count, overall and by category

```{r}
summary(bike$rented_count)
bike |> group_by(seasons) |> summarise(mean_count = mean(rented_count), n = n())
bike |> group_by(holiday) |> summarise(mean_count = mean(rented_count), n = n())
bike |> group_by(functioning_day) |> summarise(mean_count = mean(rented_count), n = n())



```

non-functioning day had zero rentals, which is self explanatory Let's filter out the non-functioning days

```{r}
bike <- bike |> filter(functioning_day == "Yes")
bike
```

The above has data for hours \[0,24) Let's aggregate hourly to daily

```{r}
daily <- bike |>
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) |>
  summarise(
    rented_count = sum(rented_count),
    rainfall = sum(rainfall),
    snowfall = sum(snowfall),
    temp = mean(temp),
    humidity = mean(humidity),
    wind_speed = mean(wind_speed),
    visibility = mean(visibility),
    dew_point_temp = mean(dew_point_temp),
    solar_radiation = mean(solar_radiation),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
daily

```

Let's summarize the daily bike data, plot

```{r}
summary(daily)

ggplot(daily, aes(x = seasons, y = rented_count)) + 
  geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(title = "Daily Bike Rentals by Season", x = "Season", y = "Total Daily Rentals")

ggplot(daily, aes(x = temp, y = rented_count, color = seasons)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  labs(title = "Daily Bike Rentals by Temperature", x = "Mean Daily Temp (C)", y = "Total Daily Rentals")

```

Let's correlate the data

```{r}

round(cor(daily |> select(where(is.numeric))),2)

```

temp vs rented_count has the highest correlation which is .75

## Let's split the data into training and testing 75/25 split using seasons as strata argument

```{r}


set.seed(558)
bike_split <- initial_split(daily, prop = 0.75, strata = seasons)
bike_train <- training(bike_split)
bike_test <- testing(bike_split)

```

## Let's add weekday/weekend factor (train & test separately)

```{r}

bike_train <- bike_train |>
  mutate(day_type = factor(if_else(wday(date) %in% c(1,7), "weekend", "weekday")))

bike_test <- bike_test |>
  mutate(day_type = factor(if_else(wday(date) %in% c(1,7), "weekend", "weekday")))

```

## Let's standardize/normalize numeric variables

```{r}

num_cols <- c("temp","humidity","wind_speed","visibility","dew_point_temp","solar_radiation","rainfall","snowfall")

train_means <- sapply(bike_train[num_cols], mean)
train_sds <- sapply(bike_train[num_cols], sd)

standardize_with <- function(df, means, sds, cols) {
  for(col in cols) {
    df[[paste0(col, "_std")]] <- (df[[col]] - means[[col]]) / sds[[col]]
  }
  df
}

bike_train <- standardize_with(bike_train, train_means, train_sds, num_cols)
bike_test <- standardize_with(bike_test, train_means, train_sds, num_cols)

```

## Fit the three models

```{r}

model1 <- lm(
  rented_count ~ temp_std + humidity_std + wind_speed_std + visibility_std + dew_point_temp_std + solar_radiation_std + rainfall_std + snowfall_std + seasons + holiday + day_type,
  data = bike_train
)

model2 <- lm(
  rented_count ~ temp_std + humidity_std + wind_speed_std + visibility_std + dew_point_temp_std + solar_radiation_std + rainfall_std + snowfall_std + seasons + holiday + day_type + seasons:holiday + seasons:temp_std + temp_std:rainfall_std,
  data = bike_train
)

model3 <- lm(
  rented_count ~ temp_std + humidity_std + wind_speed_std + visibility_std + dew_point_temp_std + solar_radiation_std + rainfall_std + snowfall_std + seasons + holiday + day_type + seasons:holiday + seasons:temp_std + temp_std:rainfall_std + I(temp_std^2) + I(humidity_std^2),
  data = bike_train
)

```

Let's write a function that does test-set RMSE for reach

```{r}
rmse <- function(model, newdata) {
  preds <- predict(model, newdata = newdata)
  sqrt(mean((newdata$rented_count - preds) ^ 2))
}

```

Now let's test the models

```{r}
rsme_tbl <- tibble(
  model = c("model1","model2","model3"),
  test_rmse = c(rmse(model1,bike_test),rmse(model2,bike_test),rmse(model3,bike_test))
)
rsme_tbl
```

model3 has the lowest RSME

Let's use this model to refit the data

## Refit the winning model(model3) on the entire data set

```{r}
full_means <- sapply(daily[num_cols], mean)
full_sds <- sapply(daily[num_cols], sd)

daily_final <- standardize_with(daily, full_means, full_sds, num_cols)

daily_final <- daily_final |>
  mutate(day_type = factor(if_else(wday(date) %in% c(1,7), "weekend", "weekday")))

daily_final

```

Let's fit the model with all of the data

```{r}

final_winning_model <- lm(
  rented_count ~ temp_std + humidity_std + wind_speed_std + visibility_std + dew_point_temp_std + solar_radiation_std + rainfall_std + snowfall_std + seasons + holiday + day_type + seasons:holiday + seasons:temp_std + temp_std:rainfall_std + I(temp_std^2) + I(humidity_std^2),
  data = daily_final
)

summary(final_winning_model)

```
